thread:
Maria: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing we split the collector hotpath into two services: collector-gateway (stateless validation/dedupe) and collector-runtime (stateful inference + KV). Goal is narrower deploy surface, faster iterations, and paying down hotpath tech debt. RFC: https://go/rdw-collector-fission
Simon: What's the latency hit for synchronous calls? another hop worries me for p50 and p95.
Maria: Benchmarks in staging: gRPC proxy +1.8ms p50, +4ms p95 when crossing pod boundary. If we colocate and use unix socket / shared-mem path it's <1ms p50. Default will be in-node for colocated pods; cross-node uses fast gRPC with keepalives.
Elaine: How do we avoid gateway becoming an SPOF? sticky routing or a sequencer? also need rollout/rollbacks spelled out.
Maria: Plan in phases:
- phase 1: gateway pass-through (validation + header tagging) — no ownership change
- phase 2: dual-write (both runtime & gateway write) + background checker
- phase 3: cutover + retire old path
Dark-launch gateway, then 5% canary, ramp. Fallback: stop sending traffic to gateway.
Nashok: KV-cache ownership is a big one. Read-after-write semantics for session state are critical. Dual-write could be racy.
Maria: Agreed. Dual-write will be gated per-tenant. We'll add a prefer-runtime header and short TTL for staging reads. Consistency checker samples mismatches and triggers reconciliation.
Kyle: Ops: more services = more infra, packing changes, autoscaling. Any cost estimates?
Maria: Small - gateway is CPU only and tiny replicas. Runtime GPU pools unchanged initially. Benefit: smaller runtime binary, faster deploys, smaller blast radius.
DevOps Bot: deploy-candidate/collector-gateway: build passed (sha: a1b2c3) — smoke ok :white_check_mark:
Liz: Customer/SLA question — any visible risk? Need comms for enterprise tenants.
Maria: Minimal in phase1. Phase3 cutover will have advisory. Suggest maintenance window only for tenants who opt into accelerated migration.
Simon: Can we do throughput soak at 5% with synthetic traffic before enabling writes? want to validate autoscaling and queuing behavior.
Maria: Yes. Soak plan: 2h run, ramp 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% in staging, verify CPU/latency, queue lengths, error budget burn.
Nashok: DB migration pattern? adding owner column seems dangerous.
Maria: DB plan:
- add nullable ingest_owner column
- dual-write populates ingest_owner for new writes
- async backfill job infers owner from last-writer heuristic
- rollback: stop gateway writes, optional clear of ingest_owner for tenants rolled back
Liz: Make sure we wire eval hooks and RDW-230 prompt regression alerts during canary.
Maria: Will do. Cutover checklist (quick):
- [ ] release gateway image to staging + smoke
- [ ] dark-launch validation traffic
- [ ] synthetic throughput soak + observability checks
- [ ] enable dual-write for pilot tenants
- [ ] run consistency checker for 48h
- [ ] backfill ingest_owner
- [ ] cutover pilot -> monitor 72h
- [ ] prepare customer communications for broad cutover
- [ ] validate rollback playbook
Maria: Anything missing? Ping me or @Maria if you want to pair on the canary run :rocket:
